title: Python: M1, an imported module-level instance (a single binding to a constructor) resolves across the import (DEC-303 (a22) item 3)
description: DEC-303 (a22) item 3, group M1, verbatim: 'M1, imported module-level instance: admitted as the (a2) 3 single binding to a constructor, carried across the import, with item 2s same-module global proviso.' Governing line (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when EVERY binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope; for a module-level name, writes through global in the same module count; a write from outside the module (m.X = ...) is the accepted blind spot. First in the DEC-303 (a23) build order after K1 and LIT (M1, R4, ALIAS, TS, Q1, then (a25), NB-b, step 5) that releases the (a36) hold on the fresh blind sample. Reuse the GCLI-108 and GCLI-109 findings: one binding enumeration (enumerableBindings) with global and nonlocal provisos; enumerate every way the module-level name can get a second binding (rebind, augmented, for, with-as, except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, import, def, class, del, global write from a function, a class body between use and binding, an annotated binding, a module-level star import) and give each its own refused fixture with a positive twin. Import forms: from m import inst (alias allowed) where m is the file that binds inst. OUT: the module-attribute form m.inst.method() (DEC-303 (a37) item 2), a re-export hop (the re-exporting module is not enumerated), and a package __init__ (A4).

acceptanceCriteria.text: an instance bound exactly once at module level of a module file to a bare-name constructor call of one in-repo class, imported directly by from m import inst (alias allowed) from the file m that binds it, resolves a method call on it to that class method, with red-before fixtures and positive and negative twins; the m.inst module-attribute form is ruled OUT (DEC-303 (a37))

each of these leaves the call unresolved, each with its own refused fixture: a second binding in the defining module by rebind, augmented assignment, for, with-as (also tuple), except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, import, from-import, def, class, tuple or star target, annotation, type alias, conditional rebind, or a global write from a function; an annotated binding; a module-level star import in the defining or the importing module; a second binding in the importing module (rebind, second import, for, def, global write, local rebind, class body); a conditional or TYPE_CHECKING import; an import of the name from a package __init__ or a package re-export; a from-import of a submodule; a re-export hop through another module (and each form of binding in the re-exporting module); a constructor that is a factory, an external class, a class with __new__, a metaclass, an opaque base or a replacing decorator, a literal, or a dotted name (Outer.Inner(), k.C()). A del is not modelled by the analyzer and has no fixture
each rule has a mutation check that goes red, and a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with any in-repo edge it creates or removes named

implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a22) item 3, M1). PROBE: before the change an imported module-level instance (from m import inst; inst.run()) was receiver-needs-inference. BUILT in src/python/calls.ts: importedInstanceClass, called from resolveAttributeCall after the 6d known-class step, one segment only. The importing name must have exactly ONE binding (enumerableBindings: a rebind, a second import of the same name, a global or nonlocal write, a for or with-as or def or any other binding, or a module-level star import in the importing module refuses), that binding a resolved from or relative import with no condition, no multiply-bound reason, a module FILE target (a package __init__ stays unresolved, A4; a from-import of a submodule is the module, not an instance). In the DEFINING module the name must have exactly one binding in module scope (global writes from functions are already on it by applyScopeRedirects), no module-level star import (starMayBind), a plain UNANNOTATED assign whose right-hand side is a call whose callee, resolved FROM the defining module, is one in-repo class passing instanceClassOf (ok MRO, no __new__, no metaclass, no opaque base, no replacing decorator: stricter than the 6d local case on purpose). Re-export hops are whatever S3 already resolves (the import target is the defining file); a rebind in the re-exporting module or an aliased re-export is refused by S3, fixtured. m.inst (module attribute access) is NOT built: the ruling text covers only the from-import carry; question put to the leader and opum-doc. modules.ts was not touched. MUTATION CHECKS (scratch python driver, replace-text mutants, each run with bun test test/python-calls.test.ts -t M1): importer count, importer enumeration (enumerableBindings to lookupBindings), reason (multiply-bound), condition, __init__ check, submodule check, star check, defining-module count, annotation check, instanceClassOf, callee scope: all 11 RED. CORPUS DIFF on the five pins (flask 49943b5a, jinja 5ef70112, httpx 7cff5f79, rich 3a109ccd, tqdm 9cf5a12b), per-site multiset diff of bin, reason and edge list, origin/dev f97d13c vs this branch: total call counts unchanged on all five; flask, jinja, httpx, tqdm: no change. rich: THREE sites receiver-needs-inference to resolved in-repo, and these are the only changes: IN-REPO EDGES CREATED: rich/color.py:552:28 STANDARD_PALETTE.match -> rich/palette.py:45:9 Palette.match; rich/color.py:565:28 WINDOWS_PALETTE.match -> rich/palette.py:45:9 Palette.match; tests/test_palette.py:6:13 STANDARD_PALETTE.__rich__ -> rich/palette.py:20:9 Palette.__rich__. All three read by hand: rich/_palettes.py binds WINDOWS_PALETTE and STANDARD_PALETTE once each to Palette(...), imported by from ._palettes import and from rich._palettes import. Receiver-to-external moves: none. Edges removed: none.

ROUND 1 FIXES (review of 8d5cb72d). B1: a re-export hop was resolved by following S3's target without enumerating the re-exporting module (S3's local-name set misses for, with-as, except-as, walrus, match, type alias, starred and list targets and global writes); fixed by option (a): importedInstanceClass refuses unless sourceModuleFile(import) equals the defining target, so only a direct from m import inst qualifies; this also refuses a package that re-exports a submodule (F4). F2, F3: only a bare-name constructor callee qualifies; Outer.Inner() and k.C() are looked up by qualname without a binding count (a gap shared with rule 6d and E1, a named follow-up, not fixed here). F5: refusal fixtures now assert no edge leaves app.py and that the call is one receiver-needs-inference (bin delta against the same files with app.py emptied), except m.inst, a call of the instance and a star import form whose bin is not receiver. The isModuleFileForName and multiply-bound reason checks were removed as redundant behind the source check (no fixture could make them red). Added fixtures: a hop through for, with-as, except-as, walrus, global in a function and in a class, match, type alias, starred and list targets, and a one-hop re-export (all refused), with the direct import as twin; a package re-export (refused) and from pkg.m import (resolves); Outer.Inner rebound, defined twice and plain; k.C() with and without a rebind; a class body in the importing module binding the name; a TYPE_CHECKING import. 11 mutants all RED. Corpus diff re-measured on the five pins after the fix: the same three rich edges, nothing else: rich/color.py:552:28 and :565:28 to rich/palette.py:45:9 Palette.match, tests/test_palette.py:6:13 to rich/palette.py:20:9 Palette.__rich__; no receiver-to-external moves.
